subject: SSQ: PII enclave routing, transient tokens & transfer handbook
messages:
From: Claire Patel <claire.patel@meridianhealth.com>

Cc: InfoSec Team <security@meridianhealth.com>

Subject: SSQ: PII enclave routing, transient tokens & transfer handbook

Hi Grace,

Thanks for taking this — Meridian is running a targeted security questionnaire for our vendor PII flows. Attached is the SSQ template (redacted) and a short list of clarifying asks from our InfoSec reviewers:

1) Can you provide a single-page data flow diagram that highlights (a) where raw identifiers enter the system, (b) where transient tokenization occurs, and (c) the boundaries of any "enclave" or processing-only zones?
2) How do you handle transient tokens / KV caches across nodes? Are they persisted to any durable store?
3) For cross-border requests, what routing and egress controls exist (region pinning, egress blocking, audit evidence)?
4) KMS custody: do you hold keys in an HSM for customer-managed keys, and can you provide a custody/rotation statement?

Our timeline is tight — can we get a draft of the diagram and short answers by EOD Wednesday (2027-05-04)? If there are design docs or example logs you can share that would speed our review.

Claire
Senior InfoSec Program Manager
Meridian Health

Claire — thanks for the clear asks. Looping in Rishi (Security/Runtime) and Kim (Privacy Ops) to help assemble answers and a compact diagram. We can meet the 2027-05-04 target with an initial package. Tonight we'll produce: 1) a one-page annotated dataflow (PDF), 2) a short matrix on token persistence, and 3) KMS custody language.

Quick expectations:
- The dataflow will show ingestion -> transient-tokenizer -> isolated inference enclave -> ephemeral KV cache -> result egress.
- Transient tokens are held in-memory by the runtime and flushed to ephemeral encrypted caches per node; durable persistence is opt-in and documented.
- Cross-border routing is region-policy driven; customers can pin processing to specific regions or block egress.

We'll attach the first-pass to a follow-up email once Rishi confirms the technical bits.

Best,

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-01T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: technical details for Meridian SSQ (PII enclave)

Grace / Kim — notes for the packet: please fold these into the matrix and diagram.

- Tokenization: We perform deterministic tokenization only when a customer enables the pseudonymization feature. Tokens are generated on ingest, stored in an in-memory KV and optionally backed up to a customer-scoped encrypted store for replay (explicit opt-in). File: transient-token-matrix.csv shows the opt-in vs default behavior.

- KV cache behavior: KV caches (per-GPU process) are encrypted with process-local keys and are not written to multi-tenant durable storage. We do rotate process keys on restart; crash-dumps do not contain raw tokens.

- Enclave boundaries: The "inference enclave" is a tenant-isolated compute pool with network egress controls and blocked admin access. We'll annotate the diagram to show: ingress load balancer (TLS), front-end validators (scrubbing), tokenizer (optional), isolated GPU pool (no shared filesystem), egress gateway (policy-enforced).

- Cross-border: Smart routing policy allows region pinning. If a customer pins to eu-west-1, requests are routed to eu capacity; fallback is documented and disabled by default. Audit logs include region, node-id, and returned model id for every request.

- KMS: For customer-managed keys we integrate with the customer's KMS (Azure Key Vault / AWS KMS / GCP KMS). We support HSM-backed key stores and can provide a custody statement and key rotation logs on request. We do not hold private key material when a customer uses CMK (bring-your-own-key).

- Evidence: We'll attach an anonymized trace snippet and redact node IDs before sharing (sample-trace.json).

I'll produce the annotated dataflow PDF and the short answers doc by EOD May 3.

Rishi
Principal Security Engineer

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: SSQ: PII enclave routing, transient tokens & transfer handbook

Hi Claire — attaching our package (attached: redwood_enclave_dataflow.pdf, transient-token-matrix.csv, ssq-answers-summary.docx). Summary below to help your reviewers skim:

- Ingest and tokenization: Raw PII may be received over TLS at the customer-dedicated endpoint. Tokenization is performed in an optional preprocessing stage; tokens are generated deterministically only when enabled by the customer. Default (no-token) path does not persist identifiers.

- KV / cache persistence: Runtime caches are in-memory and encrypted; they are not persisted to shared durable storage. Durable persistence is only used when customers opt into archive/replay and is encrypted with the customer's CMK when provided.

- Enclave and egress controls: Inference runs in tenant-isolated pools. Customers can pin regions and block failover egress. Audit logs record region, node, and model id per call.

- KMS custody: We support customer-managed keys (BYOK) with HSM-backed KMS providers; Redwood does not retain private key material for CMK customers. Rotation and custody logs can be exported for your audit.

Related links: Meridian review folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-meridian-ssq, HubSpot: HBSP-84721

If you want a short walkthrough for the review team, Rishi and I are available for a 30-minute call next week — propose Thu 2027-05-06 09:00-10:00 PT and we'll send an invite.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
